AI, Machine learning and Deep Learning

Read this as nested circles: deep learning inside machine learning inside AI. ML learns patterns from historical data and needs no explicit instructions for each task. Which statement about AI and machine learning is correct? AI, Machine learning and Deep Learning Artificial intelligence (AI) is an umbrella term for different strategies and techniques you can use to make machines more humanlike. AI includes everything from smart assistants to self-driving cars. Machine learning (ML) is one among many other branches of AI. ML is the science of developing algorithms and statistical models that computer systems use to perform complex tasks without explicit instructions. The systems rely on patterns and inference instead. Computer systems use ML algorithms to process large quantities of historical data and identify data patterns. While machine learning is AI, not all AI activities are machine learning. The seven steps are ordered. Cleaning comes before exploration, and evaluation comes before deployment. "Curious Cats Explore Fish Bowls Every Day": Collect, Clean, Explore, Features, Build, Evaluate, Deploy. In the slide's process, what comes immediately after data cleaning? List the seven steps of the data science process in order. Data Science Process 1. Data Collection: Gathering raw data from various sources (databases, APIs, sensors, etc.). 2. Data Cleaning: Handling missing data, outliers, and formatting issues. 3. Data Exploration: Analyzing data patterns, distributions, and anomalies through descriptive statistics and visualizations. 4. Feature Engineering: Transforming raw data into meaningful inputs for machine learning models. 5. Model Building: Developing predictive or inferential models using statistical learning methods. 6. Model Evaluation: Measuring model performance through metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, etc. 7. Deployment & Monitoring: Integrating the model into production and continuously monitoring performance. Chapter 2 - Part 2 Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data Instructor: Dr. Heyfa Ammar Data Science and Machine Learning Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data 1/33

Purpose In this lecture we discuss: ∙ Where to find useful data sets ∙ How to load them into Python. ∙ How to (re)structure the data ∙ How to summarize data via tables and figures Readers unfamiliar with Python are advised to read the appendix of DSML first. Python code and data sets for each chapter can be downloaded from the GitHub site: https://github.com/DSML-book Data Science and Machine Learning Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data 2/31

Data Data can be thought of as being the result of some random experiment — an experiment whose outcome cannot be determined in advance. Data are often stored in a table or spreadsheet. Convention: variables or features correspond to columns and the individual items (or units) correspond to rows. Three types of columns: ∙ One column is often an identifier or index column. ∙ Certain columns can correspond to the design of the experiment. ∙ Other columns represent the observed measurements of the experiment. Usually, these measurements exhibit variability. Data Science and Machine Learning Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data 3/33

In the nutrition data, "situation" (living alone, as a couple, with family) is best described as: Explain the difference between design variables and measurement variables with an example of each. Data Three types of columns: ∙ One column is often an identifier or index column. ∙ Certain columns can correspond to the design of the experiment. These record choices that were fixed or controlled by the experimenter before the data was collected. They describe the setup or conditions under which each observation was made, not an outcome that was measured. Example: In the nutrition_elderly example: gender or situation could be thought of as characteristics that define which group a person belongs to, rather than something being measured on them. ∙ Other columns represent the observed measurements of the experiment. Usually, these measurements exhibit variability. ○ Example: In the nutri data: height, weight, tea, coffee, age — these are measured values that vary across the 226 individuals Why the distinction matters: Design variables tell you how the data was collected or what group something belongs to: called predictors or explanatory variables Measurement variables tell you what was observed: what you're trying to explain, predict. Data Science and Machine Learning Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data 3/31

abalone.data has no header row, so header=None stops Pandas from eating the first row as column names. Why is header=None passed when reading abalone.data? Data Repositories A well-known repository of data sets is the Machine Learning Repository maintained by the University of California at Irvine (UCI): https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ These data sets are typically stored in a CSV (comma separated values) format. For example, to access the abalone data set from this website with Python, download the file to your working directory, import the pandas package via import pandas as pd and read in the data as follows: abalone = pd.read_csv('abalone.data', header = None) Data Science and Machine Learning Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data 4/31

Data Repositories Another useful repository of over 1000 data sets from various packages in the R programming language, collected by Vincent Arel-Bundock, can be found at: https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/Rdatasets/datasets.html For example, to read Fisher's famous iris data set from R's datasets package into Python, type: urlprefix = 'https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/Rdatasets/csv/' dataname = 'datasets/iris.csv' iris = pd.read_csv(urlprefix + dataname) Data Science and Machine Learning Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data 5/31

Iris Data The iris data set contains four physical measurements (sepal/petal length/width) on 50 specimens (each) of 3 species of iris: setosa, versicolor, and virginica. The output of read_csv is a DataFrame object, which is pandas's implementation of a spreadsheet. iris.head() Unnamed: 0 Sepal.Length ... Petal.Width Species 0 1 5.1 ... 0.2 setosa 1 2 4.9 ... 0.2 setosa 2 3 4.7 ... 0.2 setosa 3 4 4.6 ... 0.2 setosa 4 5 5.0 ... 0.2 setosa [5 rows x 6 columns] The names of the features can be obtained via the columns attribute of the DataFrame object, as in iris.columns. Abalone Data The first three rows of the abalone data set from the UCI repository can be found as follows: abalone.head(3) 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 0 M 0.455 0.365 0.095 0.5140 0.2245 0.1010 0.150 15 1 M 0.350 0.265 0.090 0.2255 0.0995 0.0485 0.070 7 2 F 0.530 0.420 0.135 0.6770 0.2565 0.1415 0.210 9 We can manually add the names of the features to the DataFrame by reassigning the columns attribute, as in: abalone.columns = ['Sex', 'Length', 'Diameter', 'Height', 'Whole weight', 'Shucked weight', 'Viscera weight', 'Shell weight', 'Rings'] Data Science and Machine Learning Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data 7/31

First split: does it carry numeric quantity? Then continuous (any value in a range) versus discrete (countable). The number of births in a hospital per day is: Eye color with values blue, black, brown and green is: Structuring Features According to Type Quantitative features possess “numerical quantity”, such as height, age, number of births, etc., and can either be continuous or discrete. ∙ Continuous quantitative features take values in a continuous range of possible values, such as height, voltage, or crop yield, ∙ Discrete quantitative features have a countable number of possibilities, such as a count. Qualitative features do not have a numerical meaning, but their possible values can be divided into a fixed number of categories, such as {M,F} for gender or {blue, black, brown, green} for eye color. For this reason such features are also called categorical or factors. Data Science and Machine Learning Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data 8/31

Nutrition Data When manipulating, summarizing, and displaying data, it is important to correctly specify the type of the variables (features). We illustrate this using the nutrition_elderly data set. xls = 'http://www.biostatisticien.eu/springeR/nutrition_elderly.xls' nutri = pd.read_excel(xls) This creates a DataFrame object nutri. replace swaps the codes, and astype("category") tells Pandas it is categorical. Continuous columns such as height should become float. Which line correctly recodes gender? Recoding Categorical Features We can modify the Python value and type for each categorical feature, using the replace and astype methods. For categorical features, such as gender, we can replace the value 1 with 'Male' and 2 with 'Female', and change the type to 'category' as follows. DICT = {1:'Male', 2:'Female'} # dictionary specifies replacement nutri['gender'] = nutri['gender'].replace(DICT).astype('category') The structure of the other categorical-type features can be changed in a similar way. Continuous features such as height should have type float: nutri['height'] = nutri['height'].astype(float) # Repeat this for the other variables. Summary Tables It is often useful to summarize a large spreadsheet of data in a more condensed form. A table of counts or a table of frequencies makes it easier to gain insight into the underlying distribution of a variable, especially if the data are qualitative. Such tables can be obtained with the methods describe and value_counts. Data Science and Machine Learning Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data 14/31

On a categorical column, describe reports count, unique, top and freq: 226 people, 8 fat types, sunflower most common with 68. What does describe report for a categorical column? Summarizing a Categorical Feature As an example, we load the nutri DataFrame, which we restructured and saved as 'nutri.csv', and then construct a summary for the feature (column) 'fat'. nutri = pd.read_csv('nutri.csv') nutri['fat'].describe() count 226 unique 8 top sunflower freq 68 Name: fat, dtype: object We see that there are 8 different types of fat used and that sunflower has the highest count, with 68 out of 226 individuals using this type of cooking fat. Data Science and Machine Learning Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data 15/31

value_counts The method value_counts gives the counts for the different fat types. nutri['fat'].value_counts() sunflower 68 peanut 48 olive 40 margarine 27 Isio4 23 butter 15 duck 4 colza 1 Name: fat, dtype: int64 Data Science and Machine Learning Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data 16/31

What does margins=True add to pd.crosstab? In the crosstab, 78 of 141 women and 20 of 85 men are single. State the conclusion and why you use proportions. Cross-Tabulation It is also possible to use crosstab to cross tabulate between two or more variables, giving a contingency table: pd.crosstab(nutri.gender, nutri.situation) situation Couple Family Single gender Female 56 7 78 Male 63 2 20 We see, for example, that the proportion of single men is substantially smaller than the proportion of single women. To add row and column totals, use margins=True. pd.crosstab(nutri.gender, nutri.situation, margins=True) situation Couple Family Single All gender Female 56 7 78 141 Male 63 2 20 85 All 119 9 98 226 Data Science and Machine Learning Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data 17/31

Summary Statistics: Mean In the following, x = [x₁,...,xₙ]ᵀ is a column vector of n numbers. For our nutri data, the vector x could, for example, correspond to the heights of the n = 226 individuals. The sample mean of x, denoted x̄, is simply the average of the data values: Using the mean method in Python for the nutri data, we have, for instance: nutri['height'].mean() 163.96017699115043 Data Science and Machine Learning Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data 18/31

The 0.75 sample quantile is also called: Define the p-sample quantile. Quantiles and Percentiles The p-sample quantile (0 < p < 1) of x is a value x such that at least a fraction p of the data is less than or equal to x and at least a fraction 1 − p of the data is greater than or equal to x. The sample median is the sample 0.5-quantile. The p-sample quantile is also called the 100 × p percentile. The 25, 50, and 75 sample percentiles are called the first, second, and third quartiles of the data. For the nutri data they are obtained as follows. nutri['height'].quantile(q=[0.25,0.5,0.75]) 0.25 157.0 0.50 163.0 0.75 170.0 Data Science and Machine Learning Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data 19/31

Variance is in squared units; the standard deviation is its square root, in the original units. If the sample variance is 81, what is the standard deviation? Measures of Dispersion Measures for the dispersion (spread) in the data include the sample range, maxᵢ xᵢ − minᵢ xᵢ, the sample variance s², and the sample standard deviation s = √s². nutri['height'].max() - nutri['height'].min() 48.0 round(nutri['height'].var(), 2) # round to two decimal places 81.06 round(nutri['height'].std(), 2) 9.0 Data Science and Machine Learning Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data 20/31

Note how this differs from describe on a categorical column: you get the mean, std, min, quartiles and max. describe(): Full Numeric Summary When applied to a quantitative feature, the describe method returns the minimum, maximum, mean, and the three quartiles. For example, the 'height' feature in the nutri data has the following summary statistics. nutri['height'].describe() count 226.000000 mean 163.960177 std 9.003368 min 140.000000 25% 157.000000 50% 163.000000 75% 170.000000 max 188.000000 Name: height, dtype: float64 Data Science and Machine Learning Importing, Summarizing and Visualizing Data 21/31

Visualizing Data Here, we describe various methods for visualizing data. t-SNE t-SNE (t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding) is a dimensionality reduction technique primarily used for visualizinghigh-dimensional data in lower-dimensional spaces (usually 2D or 3D). Pairwise Similarities:t-SNE calculates the pairwise similarities between data points. In the high-dimensional space, it measures how likely two points are to be neighbors based on their distances.
